findings.evidence: Line 37: `lemma circle_smul_unitDisc_zero (u : Circle) : u • (0 : Complex.UnitDisc) = 0`; naming convention says theorem names describe the conclusion outward and `_`-separated strings should correspond to definitions/connectives.
findings.fix: Rename to `circle_smul_zero`, or put it in `Complex.UnitDisc` and name it `circle_smul_zero`.
findings.issue: `circle_smul_unitDisc_zero` names the type annotation rather than the conclusion `u • 0 = 0`; Mathlib names this pattern as `smul_zero` with any disambiguating qualifier before the expression name.

findings.evidence: Line 44: `lemma circle_smul_unitDisc_eq_zero_iff (u : Circle) {z : Complex.UnitDisc} : u • z = 0 ↔ z = 0`; Mathlib already uses `Complex.UnitDisc.coe_circle_smul` for this action at `mathlib/Mathlib/Analysis/Complex/UnitDisc/Basic.lean:175`.
findings.fix: Rename to `circle_smul_eq_zero_iff`, or put it in `Complex.UnitDisc` and name it `circle_smul_eq_zero_iff`.
findings.issue: `circle_smul_unitDisc_eq_zero_iff` has the same misplaced `unitDisc` qualifier; the conclusion is `u • z = 0 ↔ z = 0`, so the standard expression name is `smul_eq_zero_iff`.

summary: The new API names insert the target type in the middle of the expression name, so the theorem names no longer read from the conclusion outward in Mathlib style.
